subject: RidgeWave POC: confirmation of success criteria + integration route plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@ridgewave.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RidgeWave POC: confirmation of success criteria + integration route plan

Alex —

Thanks again for a great demo this morning. Per our call I wanted to capture the agreed high-level success criteria and a pragmatic integration path so your engineering and procurement teams can align internally. Please review and flag any gaps.

High-level POC goals (target: 3-week evaluation window)
- Latency: end-to-end 95th percentile generation latency under 500ms for 128-token prompts (baseline traffic).
- Throughput: sustain 40 concurrent sessions with streaming responses enabled.
- Quality: automated eval pass rate >= 85% on your 120 prompt test set (we'll run these once integration is in place).
- Security: requests and KV caching remain inside your VPC for Private deployment test (if you choose Private).

Proposed technical acceptance tests (we'll own running these with your engineers):
1) SDK roundtrip and streaming sanity (SSE) for chat flow (sample app).
2) Persistent KV cache correctness for session continuation test.
3) Tool-calling sample where RidgeWave hands off a retrieval call to an internal vector DB (function-call style).

Implementation path & owners
- Week 0 (this week): Alignment and document handoff — Karthik (owner), Alex/Priya to confirm internal availability. Attached: ridgewave-poc-success-criteria.pdf
- Week 1: Integration sprint — Soojin (SE) to provide SDK snippets, API routes, and streaming examples; RidgeWave eng (Priya) to stand up the dev environment and run the SDK sample.
- Week 2: Run acceptance tests and automated evals; fix any integration regressions.
- Week 3: Final readout and decision checkpoint (POC success/next steps).

Immediate asks
- Can you confirm Priya Desai (or alternate) will be RidgeWave's technical lead for the POC?
- Any procurement/legal blockers that might push this beyond 3 weeks?

Attachments: ridgewave-poc-success-criteria.pdf, redwood-sdk-integration-checklist.xlsx

I'll follow up with a one-hour technical sync invite after I get the confirmation on owners.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@ridgewave.ai>

Subject: Re: RidgeWave POC: confirmation of success criteria + integration route plan

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear summary. Confirming Priya Desai will be our engineering lead for the POC and she'll be looped on follow-ups. High level looks good; a couple of clarifications from our side:

- For latency, we want to validate both cold-start (first request after idle) and steady-state latencies. Can Redwood provide a recommended test harness for the cold-start curve?
- For tool-calling, we need an example of how Redwood passes structured arguments and how we'd return a result (we plan to call our internal retriever service during the POC).

Procurement: our legal team needs a short, non-standard data-flow diagram showing where logs and KV cache live during the two deployment options (Hosted vs Private). They aim to sign off within 10 business days but procurement often stretches.

We'll prioritize the streaming route. Can Soojin drop the SDK streaming example (Node + Python) and a short checklist that our infra team can run?

Thanks —
Alex
Head of Product, RidgeWave
alex.morgan@ridgewave.ai

Subject: Re: RidgeWave POC: confirmation of success criteria + integration route plan

Alex / Team —

Thanks — I'm attaching a compact integration artifacts bundle (integration-snippets.zip) and a short streaming checklist. Below is a pragmatic implementation plan and the concrete API/SDK routes we recommend for the POC.

Recommended runtime paths (POC-first):
- Chat/Generation (standard): POST /v1/chat with model=redwood-large or model=redwood-s-quant for lower cost. Use token limits consistent with your test prompts.
- Generation (stateless): POST /v1/generate for single-shot generation endpoints.
- Streaming: enable SSE (EventStream) on the /v1/chat/stream route (examples included). Streaming reduces perceived latency and lets you render partial tokens in the UI.
- Tool calling / function-style handoff: we recommend the function-calling pattern where the model emits a structured JSON payload; your retriever endpoint consumes the payload and returns a result which we forward as a follow-up model input. See snippets in integration-snippets.zip (tools/ folder).
- KV cache: use our session KV with explicit write/read calls. For POC, choose ephemeral caching (48h TTL) so we can validate continuity and then discuss longer TTLs for production.

SDK specifics and snippets included in attachment (redwood-sdk-integration-checklist.xlsx):
- Node: npm install @redwood/inference@^2.1.2; code sample for chat streaming using EventSource.
- Python: pip install redwood-inference==2.1.2; async client example with streaming iterator.
- Headers: X-Redwood-Client-Id for test telemetry; include request-id for traceability.

Telemetry & acceptance hooks (what we'll measure)
- Per-request latency (client -> Redwood -> model -> client) with trace IDs.
- Token counts per response and cost estimate sample.
- Streaming completeness checks and partial-token render timing.

Owners & proposed dates
- Soojin (SE): provide attachments and run initial SDK smoke tests (deliverable: sample app + cookbooks) — by 2028-04-25.
- Priya (RidgeWave): stand up dev env, run Node + Python samples — by 2028-04-27.
- Karthik: schedule readout and procurement touchpoint — by 2028-04-29.

Attachments: integration-snippets.zip (contains code, Postman collection, tool-call examples), streaming-config.md

If you prefer, I can open a short GitHub repo with working examples and a small test harness to exercise cold-starts and steady-state.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

2) Deliverables we will provide before the sync: integration-snippets.zip, the sample app repo (private link in Drive), and the acceptance test checklist.
